note: The review date is 14 May 2024 and the forecast runs through 10 Nov 2024. Operating receipts and outflows continue at their recent rates. The company sells shares through its at-the-market program and may initiate underwritten offerings on the terms below.
narrative: {company} designs and makes radio-frequency filters; its shares trade on Nasdaq.

{claimant} sued {company} in federal court in Delaware on {commenced} for trade-secret misappropriation, patent infringement and related claims. The jury trial began on {trial_started}; on the review date it is still under way, and the company expects a verdict within days. Nothing is owed until a judgment is entered.
Before trial {claimant} itemised {claim} of damages, almost all of it one measure: the unjust enrichment of a head start built on its trade secrets.

{company} holds about {cash} of cash and owes {notes} on convertible notes. A final judgment above {threshold} left unpaid and unstayed for {days} days is a default under the notes, which lets the noteholders demand repayment. Its shares trade below the exchange's minimum bid price; the compliance deadline is {listing}.

labels.principal_measure: the claimed head-start measure of trade-secret unjust enrichment
labels.bid_price_on_review_date: $0.44, the closing price on 14 May 2024, against the $1.00 minimum bid

verdict_window.basis: Court days Thu 16 to Wed 22 May 2024, drawn uniformly per trajectory. The claimant rested on 13 May and the case was 'expected to go to the jury before the end of the week, and the jury is expected to issue a verdict in the next several days' (earnings call, 13 May 2024); jurors provided for through Fri 17 May (D.I. 550, 26 Apr 2024); trial day 7 on 14 May (minute entry). Sensitivity: the window's last day.

lower_award_amount.basis: For liability without the head-start measure, the amount is patent damages of USD 279,808 plus corrective advertising of USD 1,146,604, totalling USD 1,426,412 (D.I. 543-1 Ex. A.2 ¶¶19, 42). The USD 809,772 for poaching is a UDTPA claim; D.I. 590 (14 May 2024) held that the jury has no basis for compensable UDTPA damages, so it is excluded. USD 1,426,412 also applies where a counted component's amount is unknown. Alternatively, the amount is USD 9,999,999, just below the notes' USD 10.0M threshold.

claimant_enhancements.basis: Base: nothing added. Sensitivity: DTSA exemplary damages at the 2x cap (USD 132.2M on the USD 66.1M) plus N.C. Gen. Stat. §24-5(b) interest at 8% from 4 Oct 2021 to entry (about USD 13.9M): USD 146.1M added. Either setting leaves the award beyond cash on every trajectory.

settlement_payment.basis: The settlement amount is the company's available cash above its 30-day operating need on the settlement date, capped at the amount claimed or owed. It is paid in 12 equal monthly installments, the first on the settlement date. Installments due after 10 Nov 2024 fall outside the horizon. Alternatively, the same amount is paid in one lump sum on the settlement date.

coupon_cash_share.basis: The 15 Jun 2024 coupon, USD 1.32M, paid Mon 17 Jun. Indenture §16.02(c): paid in shares unless the company elects cash; the shares equal the payment divided by 95% of the simple average of the ten trading days' prices ending on the trading day before the interest date (here the path's share price, share_price). The resale S-3 of 13 May 2024 registers 5,000,000 Note Shares for interest and make-whole payments, and §9.02(k) caps the shares at 11,403,332; whole shares up to the 5,000,000, and the rest in cash from the available balance on the payment day (a scheduled obligation: paid in full or in arrears). At the 14 May close (USD 0.44) the coupon needs about 3.2M shares; the registered shares cover it at a ten-day price of USD 0.278 or more. Sensitivity: all cash.

rate_1961_bps_pending.basis: 28 U.S.C. §1961: the latest weekly 1-year CMT published by 14 May 2024, the week ending 10 May 2024: 5.13% (FRED WGS1YR, H.15 weekly).

ruling_lag_days.basis: One common lag for the post-trial motions (which motions will be filed is unknown before the verdict). Sensitivity: the later of two independent draws.

chips_credit_cents.basis: CHIPS tax-credit receipts are included only in the alternative that adds them to operating cash receipts; no additional receipt is booked for the dispute.

cash_facts.basis: Available cash includes receipts, obligations paid, financing proceeds, and payments on the loan and the dispute through the decision day. It determines whether a payment can be made and whether cash falls below operating need.

ordinary_view.basis: Ordinary operating risk is the same forecast with the event, including its legal costs, given no cash effect. The dispute ends on the review date at no cost, so its legal spend stops from then; operations, the line, the coupon, the cash-floor decisions and the listing chain with the notes' delisting route are the same as in the forecast.

baby_shelf.basis: Law: Form S-3 I.B.6 and SEC Securities Act Forms C&DIs 114.02 (2009), 116.22 and 116.23 (2010). I.B.1 continues until the annual update; below USD 75M public float at that update, only one third of public float may be sold under I.B.6 in twelve months. Whole underwritten takedowns must fit immediately before initiation; only completed I.B.6 sales debit later capacity. Scenario: FY2024 10-K on 6 Sep 2024, the anniversary of the FY2023 filing (akts_fy2023_10k_full); not an observed future date. The full 19 Sep 2023 proxy (akts_2023_09_19_def14a_full, pp.5-6) lists all ten directors and executive officers: Shealy, Boller, Aichele, DenBaars, Geiss, McGuire, McMahon, Neal, Petock and Rudy. They count as affiliates because they direct or manage the company; no other controlling holder is identified and the proxy knows of no holder above 5%. Their 4,101,085 beneficial shares include 1,115,154 unissued option shares and 244,922 unvested RSU shares (footnotes 4-13), leaving 2,741,009 outstanding affiliate shares. Scenario holds these affiliate holdings fixed and subtracts them from the 8 May outstanding count of 98,669,282, projecting 95,928,273 non-affiliate shares throughout the forecast; neither subsequent issuance nor vesting changes this projected float share count. The FY2023 cover's USD 148.2M non-affiliate value is a historical value, not a share count. Float uses the path price at the annual update for eligibility and the current price immediately before each later takedown for capacity. The continuous ATM offering is resized at the update to the then lawful capacity; later takedowns and actual sales reduce its remaining room, with no upward resizing inside that takedown. No pre-update I.B.1 sales count as I.B.6 sales. Pending offerings reserve room against concurrent ATM sales but are not completed sales; failure releases it.

share_ledger.basis: Authorized shares neither issued nor reserved, 175,000,000 authorized less 98,669,282 outstanding (8 May 2024), 9,341,825 reserved for conversion, 3,031,625 for options and the 5,000,000 registered for interest paid in shares = 58,957,268; an upper bound, because the equity-plan reserves are not stated (10-Q of 13 May 2024 cover and Note 16; resale S-3 of 13 May 2024). At-the-market sales and offerings draw on it; interest paid in shares draws on its own 5,000,000.

atm_pace_bps.basis: The at-the-market program re-activated on 13 May 2024 sells from 14 May on each trading day while the stock is listed and no petition has been filed, at 20% of the average daily dollar volume from 15 Mar to 14 May 2024 (close x volume over the 42 trading days of akts_daily_px.csv: USD 337,069.43), at the day's share price, net of the agents' commission (up to 3%). Proceeds settle two business days after the sale for sales before 28 May 2024 and one business day after it from that date. Whole shares a day: the day's dollar pace over the 14 May close (USD 0.44). Sensitivities: 10% and 25% of that volume.

offering_price.basis: An underwritten offering on the January 2024 terms. Gross USD 11.5M and net USD 10.4M after the underwriting discount and expenses (8-K of 29 Jan 2024). Price: the share price on the initiation day less the January offering's discount to the prior close (USD 0.50 against USD 0.7046 on 24 Jan 2024, 29.0%). The shares are the gross over the price; where the share capacity binds, the gross is the shares available times the price and the net bears the costs in proportion. Close: as many days after initiation as January's launch (preliminary prospectus supplement, 24 Jan 2024) to close (29 Jan 2024): 5.

small_claims_awarded.basis: A 'yes' to 5(a) books USD 279,808 and to 3(a) USD 1,146,604, the amounts the claimant claims (D.I. 543-1 Ex. A.2 ¶¶19, 42). Sensitivity: nothing awarded on those items.

judgment_default_reading.basis: Base: the judgment as entered. The §7.01(i) default becomes available 60 days after the Rule 62(a) automatic stay of the judgment as entered ends, where the judgment remains unpaid and undischarged and execution is not effectively stayed throughout; a post-trial ruling does not restart the period, and where it changes the judgment the holders' decision is asked again on the changed judgment. Sensitivity: the post-trial ruling, 60 days from the order disposing of the last tolling motion on the surviving amount, with no earlier opportunity.

share_price.basis: After the verdict the share price is set by a structural (Merton) model. Equity is a call on the firm's value with a strike of the notes' face plus the judgment amount owed on the day (the amount as entered, or as the post-trial ruling leaves it, less amounts paid or levied; after a settlement, its installments not yet due), over the horizon. Calibrated (KMV) on data public by 14 May 2024: the firm's value and asset volatility solve equity value = the close x shares outstanding and equity volatility = N(d1) x asset volatility x firm value / equity value. Before the verdict the price is the 14 May close. close_cents: the 14 May 2024 close, USD 0.44 (akts_daily_px_20240514). shares_outstanding: shares outstanding on 8 May 2024 (10-Q of 13 May 2024, cover). notes_face_cents: the convertible notes' principal, USD 44.0M. rate_bps: the 1-year U.S. Treasury par yield on 14 May 2024, 5.16% (U.S. Treasury, Daily Treasury Par Yield Curve Rates, 2024; home.treasury.gov). price_table: equity volatility, the annualised (x 252) sample standard deviation of the daily log returns of the closes over the 240 trading days of the table (1 Jun 2023 to 14 May 2024). horizon_years: one year.

offering_materiality.basis: The company initiates an underwritten offering only where its net proceeds, limited by the share capacity left, cover the shortfall of available cash below its operating need for the next month. Available cash is measured at the end of the decision day after any levy served that day. Where cash covers the need, any available offering can be initiated. Alternatively, any available offering can be initiated regardless of whether its proceeds cover the shortfall.

offering_lockup.quote: For a period commencing on the date hereof and ending on the 90th day after the closing of the Offering (the “Lock-Up Period”), the Company agrees not to, directly or indirectly, without the prior written consent of the Representative, (1) offer for sale, sell, pledge or otherwise dispose of [...] any shares of Common Stock
offering_lockup.basis: The underwriting agreement of 25 Jan 2024 with Roth Capital Partners (Exhibit 1.1 to the 8-K of 29 Jan 2024), §4(l) Company Lock-Up. The exceptions (A)-(H) cover the offered shares, employee plans, the notes' conversion and interest shares, the S-8, the TST acquisition shares and strategic issuances; none covers at-the-market sales, and the 424B5 of 29 Jan 2024 says the program may resume 'subject to any applicable lock-up restrictions in the Underwriting Agreement'. Applied to an offering on the path: the at-the-market sales pause from its pricing (the underwriting agreement's date, one day after launch as in January: 24 to 25 Jan 2024) to its close, and where it closes, through the 90th day after the close.

verdict_form.source: D.I. 580, the final special verdict form filed 9 May 2024 (RECAP gov.uscourts.ded.76727.580.0), read with the claimant's proposed form D.I. 535 (12 Apr 2024), which puts the same claims in the order trade secrets, UDTPA, false advertising, conspiracy, patent.

q1a.quote: Has Qorvo established by the greater weight or preponderance of the evidence that (a) this alleged trade secret qualifies as a trade secret and (b) Akoustis is liable for trade secret misappropriation for this trade secret? / Has Qorvo established by a greater weight or preponderance of the evidence that Akoustis was unjustly enriched by misappropriating this trade secret?
q1a.asks: whether the jury answers “YES” in both columns for at least one alleged trade secret (the form's gate: “IF YOU ANSWERED “YES” IN BOTH COLUMNS FOR ANY ALLEGED TRADE SECRET IN QUESTION 1(a), THEN ANSWER QUESTIONS 1(b) AND 1(c)”)

plain.asks: whether the jury finds {company} liable for misappropriating at least one of {claimant}'s trade secrets and unjustly enriched by it

q1b.quote: State the amount Akoustis was unjustly enriched by misappropriating Qorvo’s trade secrets as to which you have answered “Yes” and “Yes” in Question 1(a) above.

plain.asks: the amount of the jury's award for unjust enrichment on the trade-secret claim

q1c.quote: Was Akoustis’s misappropriation of any of Qorvo’s trade secrets as to which you answered “Yes” and “Yes” in Question 1(a) above willful and malicious?

plain.asks: whether the jury finds the misappropriation willful and malicious

q1d.quote: What amount of exemplary damages, if any, do you award to Qorvo against Akoustis?

plain.asks: the amount of exemplary damages, at most twice the unjust-enrichment award (18 U.S.C. §1836(b)(3)(C))

q2a.quote: Has Qorvo proven by a preponderance of the evidence its Civil Conspiracy claim against Akoustis?

plain.asks: whether the jury finds the civil conspiracy claim proven

q2b.quote: Do you find that Qorvo has proven by a preponderance of the evidence that actual damage to Qorvo was caused by the conspiracy?

plain.asks: whether the jury finds the conspiracy caused {claimant} actual damage

q2c.quote: What amount of damages for actual loss, if any, were caused by Akoustis’ action and thus you award to Qorvo against Akoustis?

plain.asks: the amount of the jury's award for actual loss on the conspiracy claim

q3a.quote: Has Qorvo proven by a preponderance of the evidence each of the elements of its False Advertising claim against Akoustis?

plain.asks: whether the jury finds the false-advertising claim proven

q5a.quote: Do you find that Qorvo has proven by a preponderance of the evidence that the claims of the ’018 or the ’755 Patents have been infringed?
q5a.asks: whether the jury answers “YES” for at least one patent claim

plain.asks: whether the jury finds at least one patent claim infringed

collapsed.quote: Has Qorvo proven by a preponderance of the evidence its Unfair and Deceptive Trade Practices Act claim against Akoustis?
collapsed.why: D.I. 590 (14 May 2024): “The jury has no reasonable basis to find compensable damages under the UDTPA”. Liability alone carries no money.

collapsed.quote: Did Qorvo prove by a preponderance of the evidence that Akoustis’ infringement of the ’018 or ‘755 patent was willful?
collapsed.why: 5(b) is an amount (inside the lower branch's bounded amount); willfulness only lets the court enhance patent damages later (35 U.S.C. §284), inside the same bound. Neither changes a verdict branch.

verdict_form.amounts: The award is the sum of the items the jury finds: 3(a) books the corrective-advertising amount and 5(a) the patent amount Qorvo claims (D.I. 543-1 Ex. A.2 ¶¶19, 42: USD 1,146,604 and USD 279,808; nothing where the parameter small_claims_awarded is false); 3(a) and 5(a) are asked wherever the total stays below the J1b top line. The amount items 1(b), 1(d) and 2(c) are asked as thresholds on the total judgment's lines (nothing, the reach line, the top line, one further cut in each band below the top line, and USD 10,000,000 wherever a band would straddle it), each conditional on the band established; a band below the top line books its midpoint and the band above it the claimant's amount (USD 67,526,412). 1(c) and 1(d) are asked only where exemplary damages (at most twice 1(b)) can move the total across a line.

assumption_variants.note: Each alternative changes one setting from the central case. All other settings remain the same.

variants.label: Operating burn 30% lower from 15 May 2024, instead of the recent run rate
variants.note: Changes the company's operating outflows. Central: the bank feed's recent flows continue. Alternative: the cut the company announced on its 13 May 2024 earnings call, a 30% lower operating burn in the June quarter, taken off every operating outflow except legal costs and debt service.

variants.label: Equity: $5.0M received on 14 Jun 2024, instead of none booked
variants.note: Central: no financing is booked beyond the company's at-the-market sales and offerings it initiates. Alternative: $5.0M of new equity received on 14 Jun 2024.

variants.label: Settlement paid at once, instead of in 12 monthly installments
variants.note: Changes when a settlement's money leaves the company. Central: the settlement amount (the company's cash above its 30-day operating need, capped at the amount claimed) paid in 12 equal monthly installments, since a distressed company does not pay out its runway at once. Alternative: the same amount in one payment on the settlement date.

variants.label: Collection: only from cash above 30 days of operating need, instead of each installment in full when cash covers it
variants.note: Changes how Slope collects. Central: Slope's automatic debit takes each installment in full on its due date when the company's cash covers it. Alternative: the company holds back its next 30 days of operating need, and Slope collects only from cash above that.

variants.label: Cash floor: 60 days of operating outflows, instead of 30
variants.note: Changes the cash level at which the company decides whether to initiate an offering, file, or do neither, and the cash it counts as available for a settlement or security. Slope's debit does not read it, so collections change only through those decisions.

variants.label: June notes coupon paid in cash, instead of in shares
variants.note: Changes how the company pays the $1.32M notes coupon due 15 Jun 2024. Central: in shares, which the notes allow unless the company elects cash, and which its registered shares cover. Alternative: all in cash.

variants.label: Share sales on the market: 10% of recent trading volume a day, instead of 20%
variants.note: Changes the cash the company raises by selling shares on the market. Central: from 14 May, 20% of the average daily dollar volume of 15 Mar to 14 May 2024 (about $67,400 a trading day) at the 14 May close, less a 3% commission. Alternative: 10%.

variants.label: Share sales on the market: 25% of recent trading volume a day, instead of 20%
variants.note: Changes the cash the company raises by selling shares on the market. Central: 20% of the average daily dollar volume of 15 Mar to 14 May 2024. Alternative: 25%.

variants.label: General nonpayment under the notes: judged over 15 days, instead of 30
variants.note: Changes when the notes fall due because the company generally is not paying its debts. Central: unpaid bills outstanding throughout the last 30 days, and at least a quarter of what fell due in them left unpaid. Alternative: over 15 days.

variants.label: General nonpayment under the notes: judged over 60 days, instead of 30
variants.note: Changes when the notes fall due because the company generally is not paying its debts. Central: over the last 30 days. Alternative: over 60 days.

variants.label: General nonpayment under the notes: half of what fell due left unpaid, instead of a quarter
variants.note: Changes when the notes fall due because the company generally is not paying its debts. Central: at least a quarter of the bills that fell due in the last 30 days left unpaid. Alternative: at least half.

variants.label: Jury: nothing awarded on the patent and advertising claims when it finds them, instead of the amounts claimed
variants.note: Changes what the jury awards if it finds for {claimant} on patent infringement or false advertising. Central: the amounts {claimant} claims for them ($279,808 and $1,146,604). Alternative: nothing.

variants.label: Notes' judgment default: counted from the post-trial ruling, instead of from the judgment's entry
variants.note: Changes when an unpaid judgment becomes a default under the notes. Central: 60 days after the judgment's automatic 30-day stay ends. Alternative: 60 days after the court rules on the last post-trial motion, on the amount that survives.

assumption_variants.central_note: Settings every outcome shares: the bank feed's recent flows continue, the company sells shares on the market at 20% of recent daily trading volume, no other financing is booked unless the company initiates an offering, the cash floor is 30 days of operating outflows, and Slope collects each installment by automatic debit.
